# Data

The data come from a mouse **backcross** with 103 individuals. Each was genotyped at 14 markers (M1-M14) along one chromosome and weighed (body weight, `BW`). In a backcross each marker has only two genotype classes, coded here as 0 and 1.

The first row of the file is a placeholder with no body weight, so it is dropped.

```{r load}
mouse <- read.csv("../data/mouse.csv")
mouse <- mouse[-1, ]
markers <- paste0("M", 1:14)
dim(mouse)
head(mouse)
```

# Genotype heatmap

Each column of the image is an individual and each row a marker. Long runs of one colour are chromosome segments inherited intact. A colour change marks a **crossover** between two neighbouring markers.

```{r heatmap, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
image(as.matrix(mouse[, markers]),
      col = c("#d7191c", "#2c7bb6"),
      main = "Mouse backcross: genotypes at 14 markers",
      xlab = "Individual", ylab = "Marker", axes = FALSE)
```

# Genotype counts: `for` and `while` loops

Both loops print the genotype frequencies at each marker, so you can see the same task written two ways.

```{r loops}
for (m in markers) {
  cat(m, ":", table(mouse[[m]]), "\n")
}

i <- 1
while (i <= length(markers)) {
  cat(markers[i], ":", table(mouse[[markers[i]]]), "\n")
  i <- i + 1
}
```

The vectorised alternative returns the same counts as one tidy table:

```{r sapply}
t(sapply(mouse[, markers], table))
```

# Single-marker regression

Is body weight associated with the genotype at M1? A linear model `BW ~ M1` tests whether the two genotype classes differ in mean weight.

```{r regression}
reg1 <- lm(BW ~ M1, data = mouse)
summary(reg1)
```

```{r boxplot, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 4}
boxplot(BW ~ M1, data = mouse,
        names = c("M1 = 0", "M1 = 1"),
        col = c("#fdae61", "#abd9e9"),
        ylab = "Body weight", main = "Body weight by M1 genotype")
```

Repeating the test at every marker gives a simple genome scan. This is the idea behind *single-marker analysis* in QTL mapping (see report 04).

```{r scan, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
p_values <- sapply(markers, function(m) {
  anova(lm(mouse$BW ~ mouse[[m]]))[["Pr(>F)"]][1]
})

plot(seq_along(markers), -log10(p_values), type = "b", pch = 19,
     xaxt = "n", xlab = "Marker", ylab = expression(-log[10](p)),
     main = "Single-marker scan for body weight")
axis(1, at = seq_along(markers), labels = markers, las = 2)
abline(h = -log10(0.05 / length(markers)), col = "red", lty = 2)
legend("topright", "Bonferroni 5 %", col = "red", lty = 2, bty = "n")
```
